title: Replacing a language leaves stale extension mappings
reasoning: Registration overwrites an existing language specification but only adds extension mappings. If the replacement removes an extension, that extension still resolves to the replacement specification even though it no longer supports it. The name and extension registries consequently disagree.
reproduction: Register a language with extensions ['.foo', '.bar'], then register the same name with a specification supporting only ['.foo']. Looking up '.bar' still returns the replacement specification.
recommendation: Define duplicate registration behavior explicitly: reject duplicate names before mutation, or remove mappings owned by the replaced language before installing its new extensions.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise slop_code.agent_runner.registry, a different registry; they do not exercise language registration or extension lookup.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test registry consistency across repeated registration: either assert duplicate registration fails without changing either mapping, or assert replacement removes obsolete extensions, retains current extensions, and preserves mappings owned by other languages.
minimumFixScope: Update register_language and add behavioral coverage for language registry consistency.
